item: The findings of the coordinator's check of #1292: a failed call is not in the browse report, the latency summary builds its rows outside the lock record takes, the durable search-timing lines stop repeating their static text, and three paths gained a test
key_paths: src/monitoring/latency.py; src/monitoring/search_timing.py; src/monitoring/release_run.py; src/monitoring/secret_scrub.py; tests/test_latency_attribution.py; tests/test_search_timing_browse.py; tests/test_release_run.py; tests/test_malloc_arena_default.py; tests/test_kpi_k2_attribution.py; docs/product/RELEASE_0.4_GATE.md; docs/ledger/SHIPPED_LOG.md
summary: #1292 was merged before the coordinator's check of it ended, so its findings ride the next PR. The browse report's method text now says what the code does: a call that failed is not in it (the route latency log counts those) and a call for a fixed set of ids is not timed. latency.summary() built every route's row (three sorts of a window of up to 512) while holding the lock record() takes on the event-loop thread; it now copies each route under the lock and builds the rows after releasing it (300 routes with full windows: about 38 ms of row-building outside the lock, the copies holding it about 4 ms in the measurement here), with a test that the rows are built unlocked and one that a request recorded meanwhile does not change a row already copied, both failing on the old code. N3: the two durable search-timing logs wrote the same method and caveat words on every line and nothing reads them back, so a line is now the measurement only, as the coordinator's note of 03:49 asked (the report carries the words once per kind, as record_method and record_caveat of the text aggregate and of browse: the first wording said the report already held them, which was untrue of the phase names and the clock's edges, and the coordinator's check of that moved them into the report, from one constant the record and the report share): a browse line went from about 1,940 to about 195 bytes (the log at its 5,000-line cap from 9.7 to 0.98 MB) and a text line from about 1,040 to about 190 bytes (5.2 to 0.95 MB), and the cut of 5,250 lines, which rewrites the whole file on the request thread every 250th append, from 39-97 ms to 2.3-4.7 ms for a browse log and from 12-16 ms to 2.2-3.9 ms for a text log (medians of seven cuts, the whole set taken twice, warm cache, the module's own writer and cut: the one set, which the log's docstring quotes, where single figures from two sessions had disagreed with its range). The in-process window keeps the whole record, the caller's dict is never cut, a log written before holds both shapes until the cuts drop the older one, and the durable summary says so; the schema string stays because no key a reader uses moves. The log docstring quotes the sizes and times before and after, the page-size bound says what it protects, and the cache-off count phase and the tie between UNLOCK_ROUTES and the unlock router's own routes are tested. Ledger text: the #1292 row says K2's formula is unchanged (not its value) and names both of its lessons, the gate's row D sentence no longer attributes to Q117 a rule it does not state, and row A says a later judging attempt, an own one or an imported one, makes the verdict read measured. Five small findings of the same check ride along: the passphrase is out of what ANY phase's exception says in the report, the state file and the log (the error log keeps a traceback's tail in app_errors.jsonl, which a bundle carries), a child that cannot be started leaves no empty install directory, a comment and a docstring no longer overclaim, and the number and tunables rules of the allocator reading are now also checked against a real glibc child, 29 shapes, where fakes alone had pinned them (of the preload rules, a preload that is no allocator and one that does not load run as real children; a replaced malloc is a stand-in library the loader really loads, and a real jemalloc where the machine has one). The Opus read of 87e5284e added a test that a summary row's status map is a copy a later call cannot change, and the browse report's method text now says that a call which fails after its query returned the page, while its response is built, is in the report and one which fails before is not, pinned by running the handler. The coordinator's check of the next head added: the passphrase is also out of what the P0 phase catches (with the release-run row), a failure that wraps another is scrubbed from its whole traceback and tested for both chains, the table's negative-number row was wrong and the arena rows are told apart where the default limit bites (with the allocator row), the Ollama install script is named a deliberate non-member of the three spawners, and a repr of the run's parameters no longer prints the passphrase.
